worker_target_description: Study 1 replication of hypothetical donations: unresolved selection between explicit-learning main effect H3a and Identifiability × Explicit Learning interaction H2a, both without joint condition (Table 8); H1a is also present in the broad locator.
worker_notes: Identity independently verified from the supplied full journal-report text: title Revisiting and Rethinking the Identifiable Victim Effect: Replication and Extension of Small, Loewenstein, and Slovic (2007); authors Maximilian Maier, Yik Chun Wong, Gilad Feldman; DOI 10.1525/collabra.90203. Header citation says 2024, matching the neutral reference, while journal issue is Vol. 9, Issue 1, 2023; this internal date discrepancy is preserved. Text comprises 21 pages including methods, results, references, and supplementary-material links, rather than an abstract or preregistration. No local PDF was supplied; no acquisition performed. Original side is an unassigned placeholder, not an assessment of original-source availability. The broad description and p.12/Table 8 locator do not distinguish H2a (Identifiability × Explicit Learning interaction without joint) from H3a (Explicit Learning main effect without joint). Both concern donations and analytical/explicit learning in the Study 1 replication. No hypothesis identifier or contrast is supplied. Do not choose by table order or numerical agreement. Printed same-test candidates (Table 8): H2a F = 0.654, p = .419 (equality); H3a F = 0.89, p = .346 (equality). A broader identifiable-victim main-effect reading would instead select H1a F = 0.01, p = .923, reinforcing the insufficient specificity. No candidate selected as a positive effect/p extraction. For the common Study 1 ANOVA, p.10 explicitly identifies the four cells Identifiable-Explicit, Statistical-Explicit, Identifiable-Control, Statistical-Control. Table 5 p.9 prints respective participant counts 170, 159, 165, 176. Candidate analytic N = 170 + 159 + 165 + 176 = 670 mutually exclusive participants; joint groups 173 and 161 are excluded by design, not exclusion criteria. P.6 states full-sample analyses were used and 56 exclusion-eligible responses were retained in main analyses; post-exclusion analyses are supplemental. N=1004 in Table 8 note is the unified experiment total, not the four-cell Study 1 test sample. Because target correspondence remains unresolved, N is retained only as a model candidate in this note and n disposition, as instructed. Authors report no support for H1a, H2a, H3a, with an explicit failure-to-replicate conclusion for H1a/H2a; reported_success records this common narrative verdict independently of the unresolved coefficient selection.
